name: Tonga
prevalence_note: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga has issued a run of public warnings: on 3 December 2025 and again with New Zealand's Financial Markets Authority on 10 February 2026 it described a Ponzi-style cryptocurrency scheme circulating in Tonga and among Tongan communities abroad; on 17 April 2026 it said romance scams were continuing to rise; on 21 April 2026 it said Ponzi and pyramid-type schemes were rising and were often promoted through social media, messaging apps, churches, workplaces and family networks; and on 20 November 2026 it warned of an online promotion that misused Tonga Communications Corporation branding to collect personal and banking information.
cross_border_note: The joint NRBT and FMA notice says the crypto scheme has been aimed at Tongan communities in Tonga, New Zealand, Australia and the United States, and that related clone platforms had been listed by the FMA. The romance notice also warns that caller ID can be spoofed to look local. A +676 number or a familiar telecom logo is not proof of a genuine Nuku'alofa institution.

scams.name: Social-media crypto trading group with a fake app and a withdrawal fee
scams.name_en: NRBT and FMA warnings, 2025-2026: a Ponzi-style cryptocurrency scheme promoted in WhatsApp, Viber or similar groups, using a fake trading app, promised very high returns, recruitment of family and friends, and a fee that is said to be required before funds can be withdrawn
context_keywords: WhatsApp or Viber investment group for Tongans
transfer crypto into a trading app
promised return of one hundred percent
fee required before a full withdrawal

red_flag_keywords.text: join this group, the return is guaranteed
move your crypto from the exchange into our app
pay a fee or tax before you can withdraw
bring in family or church members to earn more

scams.signals_en: NRBT and FMA (2025-2026) warned of Facebook, WhatsApp and Viber crypto Ponzi/pyramid groups promising huge returns, recruitment bonuses and fake trading apps (some with malware), blocking withdrawals to demand extra taxes or fees.
scams.legit_en: Under Tonga's Banking Act 2020, taking public funds for investment or lending requires an NRBT banking licence. Licensed firms never mandate unofficial trading apps, recruiting relatives, or withdrawal fees; crypto lacks legal protection.
bait_tactics: Refuse to download an unofficial trading app, to send crypto into it, or to pay a fee that is said to unlock a withdrawal.
Ask whether the person or firm holds an NRBT banking licence, and why a lawful investment would need recruitment of family, church or workplace contacts.
Tell anyone already involved to keep records and to raise the matter with their bank, with NRBT or with the Tonga Police Cybercrime Unit, as the Bank advises.

scams.name: Romance approach that later asks for emergency, travel or package money
scams.name_en: NRBT 17 April 2026 public notice: romance scams that build a fast online relationship, then ask for money for a fake emergency, medical bill, travel, a package or gift, or a business partnership, often after moving the chat to WhatsApp or Viber
context_keywords: fast declaration of love after a short chat
person claims to work overseas and avoids a video call
move from Facebook Messenger to WhatsApp or Viber
send crypto or a gift card for a package or fare

red_flag_keywords.text: I love you, please send money for an emergency
pay a fee before the gift or package can be released
chip in as a partner in this business
leave Messenger and continue on WhatsApp or Viber

scams.signals_en: On 17 Apr 2026 NRBT warned of romance scams: fast love confessions, overseas worker stories avoiding cameras, pressure to move to WhatsApp/Viber, and requests for crypto or gift cards for emergencies, gifts, travel or business deals.
scams.legit_en: A genuine relative, partner or business contact in Tonga never demands crypto or gift cards to release a parcel, and banks never ask you to send card details to an online courtship contact. NRBT warns against sending money or IDs.
bait_tactics: Refuse to send money, card details, a passport image or a fee for a gift, fare or medical story to someone who has not been met in person.
Decline to move the conversation onto a private app solely at the other person's insistence, and treat a refusal to use a camera as a warning sign from the Bank's list.
If money may already have been sent, contact the bank to protect the accounts and report the matter to the Tonga Police Cybercrime Unit.

scams.name: Fake TCC Constitution Day gift questionnaire collecting bank data
scams.name_en: NRBT 20 November 2026 warning: an online promotion misuses Tonga Communications Corporation branding, offers a Constitution Day gift after a questionnaire, collects personal and banking information, and has already been linked to internet-banking losses
context_keywords: telecom logo on a social-media prize post
form that asks for banking information
link said to be from Tonga Communications Corporation

red_flag_keywords.text: complete this TCC gift questionnaire with your bank details
Constitution Day prize if you open this unofficial link
enter internet-banking data to claim the telecom gift
TCC branding on a page that is not the official telecom site

scams.signals_en: On 20 Nov 2026 NRBT warned of a social-media scam misusing Tonga Communications Corporation (TCC) branding as a Constitution Day cash-gift questionnaire to harvest personal and internet-banking data, already hitting several bank accounts.
scams.legit_en: Tonga Communications Corporation never needs customer internet-banking details in a social-media questionnaire for a real promotion. Genuine telecom or bank issues use published channels, not unofficial prize forms with copied logos.
bait_tactics: Do not fill in a Constitution Day or telecom gift form that asks for personal or banking information, and do not follow the accompanying link.
Treat copied TCC branding on a social-media post as a reason to stop, and check any real offer only on the telecom's own published site.
If a form may already have been completed, contact the customer's bank immediately about internet banking, and report the promotion to Tonga Police, as NRBT advises.
